prs.title: [compiler] Type react-native PanResponder.create to fix react-hooks/refs false positive
prs.author: Gourav224
prs.body:
Fixes #37955

**Depends on #37975** (retains declared `Freeze` effects for already-frozen values, as suggested by @javache). Until that merges this PR's diff also shows its commit.

## Summary

`react-hooks/refs` reports "Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render" for callbacks passed to React Native's `PanResponder.create({...})`, because the compiler treats `PanResponder` imported from `react-native` as an unknown function that may call its arguments during render. `PanResponder.create()` only stores the handlers and invokes them later from gesture events.

The compiler already has a signature for exactly this (`PanResponder.create` freezes its config and doesn't call it during render), but it only exists in the test-only `shared-runtime` type provider in `snap`, so real code never gets it. This adds the same signature for `react-native` to `defaultModuleTypeProvider` (TypeScript, and the Rust port in `default_module_type_provider.rs`), so the callbacks are treated as deferred, like the `IntersectionObserver` fix in #37764.

Other unknown functions still report errors when given ref-accessing callbacks.

## How did you test this change?

Added a valid case to `packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/__tests__/ReactCompilerRuleTypescript-test.ts` (the repro shape from the issue). Snap fixtures can't cover this because `snap` replaces the module type provider with its own.

- Without the fix: `cd packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks && npx jest ReactCompilerRuleTy

prs.title: [compiler] Allow ref access in PerformanceObserver / ReportingObserver callbacks
prs.author: zhoubiao188
prs.body:
## Summary

`new PerformanceObserver(cb)` and `new ReportingObserver(cb)` are compiled with a false positive when the callback touches a ref:

```
Error: Cannot access refs during render
  4 |   return new PerformanceObserver(() => {
    |                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render
```

Both constructors only *retain* the callback and invoke it asynchronously once the observation fires — never during render — so reading (or writing) a ref from the callback is safe. `IntersectionObserver` (#37764) and `ResizeObserver` / `MutationObserver` (#37895) are already modelled exactly this way; these two were just missed and fall back to the unknown-constructor default, whose `Freeze` on the callback trips `ValidateNoRefAccessInRender`.

This is the same class of fix as #37895, which is now on `main`.

## Fix

Add both to `TYPED_GLOBALS` (TypeScript) and `build_typed_globals` (Rust) using the same signature shape as the existing observers:

| Global | Constructor signature |
| --- | --- |
| `PerformanceObserver` | `(callback)` → `[Freeze]` |
| `ReportingObserver` | `(callback, options)` → `[Freeze, Read]` |

`ReportingObserver`'s second argument is a genuine constructor argument (unlike the observers whose options belong to `observe()`), so it is read rather than retained.

Both backends are updated so TS and Rust stay in parity.

prs.title: [compiler] Preserve signed zero in constant propagation and code generation
prs.author: chengchuu
prs.body:
## Summary Fixes #37994 The TypeScript and Rust compilers lose the distinction between `0` and `-0` when merging branch constants and generating code. This can make `1 / value` return the wrong infinity. To reproduce, compile this component and toggle `condition`: ```jsx function Component({condition}) { let value; if (condition) { value = 0; } else { value = -0; } return
{1 / value}
; } ``` The result should alternate between `Infinity` and `-Infinity`, but the compiled component keeps returning `Infinity`. Both backends now preserve signed zero when merging constants and emit negative zero explicitly. NaN merging behavior and JavaScript equality semantics remain unchanged. ## How did you test this change? On macOS arm64 with Rust installed through Homebrew, I first created a Cargo symlink for the path used by `test-babel-ast.sh`: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.cargo/bin ln -s /opt/homebrew/opt/rustup/bin/cargo ~/.cargo/bin/cargo ``` I then manually ran these commands from the repository root: ```bash cd compiler yarn install --frozen-lockfile cargo test --workspace --locked yarn snap:build yarn snap yarn snap --rust cd .. bash compiler/scripts/test-babel-ast.sh ``` Rust workspace tests and Babel AST/scope checks passed. All tests in the full compiler snapshot suite passed on both TypeScript and Rust backends. The selected fixtures also passed runtime evaluation on each backend.

prs.title: [DOM] Use SyntheticTransitionEvent for onTransitionRun, onTransitionStart, and onTransitionCancel
prs.author: ShakilUrRehman21
prs.body:
Fixes #37984

## Summary

When support for CSS transition events (`onTransitionRun`, `onTransitionStart`, `onTransitionCancel`) was added in #27345 alongside `onTransitionEnd`, the events were registered as simple events in `DOMEventProperties.js` and defined in `DOMEventNames.js`, but they were not added to the switch statement in `SimpleEventPlugin.js`.

As a result, while `onTransitionEnd` uses `SyntheticTransitionEvent`, `onTransitionRun`, `onTransitionStart`, and `onTransitionCancel` were defaulting to base `SyntheticEvent`. Because `SyntheticEvent` does not implement `TransitionEventInterface`, properties such as `propertyName`, `elapsedTime`, and `pseudoElement` were not normalized onto the synthetic event object, evaluating to `undefined`.

This PR:
1. Imports `TRANSITION_CANCEL`, `TRANSITION_RUN`, and `TRANSITION_START` into `SimpleEventPlugin.js`.
2. Adds cases for them in `extractEvents` so they instantiate `SyntheticTransitionEvent`.
3. Adds a regression test suite `SyntheticTransitionEvent-test.js` validating property normalization across all four transition events.

## How did you test this change?

- Added `packages/react-dom/src/events/__tests__/SyntheticTransitionEvent-test.js` covering `onTransitionEnd`, `onTransitionRun`, `onTransitionStart`, and `onTransitionCancel` (fails on `main` with `propertyName: undefined` and passes with this fix).

prs.title: [RN] Call dispatchNativeEvent when the event target is null
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

With `enableNativeEventTargetEventDispatching` on, the Fabric renderer skipped `dispatchNativeEvent` when the touched view had already unmounted, so the touch end never reached the JS responder and the next tap got lost. This passes the null target through instead, so React Native can still release the responder. It needs react/react-native#59522 to land first, since `dispatchNativeEvent` there throws on a null target today.

Fixes #38006

## How did you test this change?

Added a test in `ReactFabric-test.internal.js` that unmounts a view, dispatches a touch end to its old instance handle, and expects `dispatchNativeEvent` to get a null target. It fails on main and passes with this change. Also ran `yarn test packages/react-native-renderer` (default, `--prod`, www-modern), `yarn flow fabric`, `yarn linc` and `yarn prettier-check`.
